hints: Square both non-negative moduli to obtain an ordinary quadratic inequality.
Factor the quadratic, order its two zeros, and use a sign chart to select the outside intervals with strict endpoints.
walkthrough:
Square both sides of $|3x + 2| < 3|2x - 1|$ since both sides are non-negative:
$$(3x + 2)^2 < 3^2(2x - 1)^2$$
$$(3x + 2)^2 < 9(2x - 1)^2$$

Rearrange into a single quadratic inequality:
$$9x^2 + 12x + 4 < 36x^2 - 36x + 9$$
$$0 < (36x^2 - 9x^2) + (-36x - 12x) + (9 - 4)$$
$$27x^2 - 48x + 5 > 0$$

Find the critical values by factoring the quadratic $27x^2 - 48x + 5 = 0$:
$$\text{Product } = 27 \times 5 = 135, \quad \text{Sum } = -48 \implies \text{Factors: } -45 \text{ and } -3$$
$$27x^2 - 45x - 3x + 5 = 9x(3x - 5) - 1(3x - 5) = (9x - 1)(3x - 5) = 0$$
$$9x - 1 = 0 \implies x = \dfrac{1}{9}$$
$$3x - 5 = 0 \implies x = \dfrac{5}{3}$$

Determine the solution set for the strict inequality $(9x - 1)(3x - 5) > 0$:
$$\text{Since the parabola opens upwards, the expression is strictly positive outside the roots:}$$
$$x < \dfrac{1}{9} \quad \text{or} \quad x > \dfrac{5}{3}$$
